title: AI-Driven Fraud Detection Using Self-Supervised Deep Learning for Enhanced Customer Identity Modeling
venue: International Journal of Humanities and Information Technology
tldr: Self-supervised deep learning combining contrastive learning, temporal transformers, and graph neural networks achieves 0.96 F1-score on imbalanced financial fraud detection with 35 million transactions.
problem_and_motivation: Traditional rule-based and supervised fraud detection systems depend on manually constructed features and large quantities of labeled fraud data, making them ineffective against evolving adaptive fraud patterns.
approach: Self-supervised pretraining via contrastive behavioral representation learning and masked feature reconstruction learns discriminative customer behavior embeddings from unlabeled transaction data.
A Temporal Transformer module captures sequential spending patterns, velocity changes, and temporal anomalies across transaction histories using multi-head self-attention.
A Graph Neural Network combining GraphSAGE and GAT models cross-account identity relationships through shared devices, IP addresses, and merchants to identify fraud rings and mule networks.
A stacked ensemble of XGBoost, deep neural networks, and logistic regression meta-learner fuses temporal, identity, and self-supervised embeddings for real-time risk scoring.
Focal loss and dynamic thresholding address extreme class imbalance, with cost-sensitive learning penalizing missed fraudulent transactions more heavily.
Evaluation conducted on 35.2 million real-world transactions with 95,312 confirmed fraud cases across 187 feature dimensions.
Ablation studies systematically isolate contributions of individual self-supervised learning components and GNN-based identity modeling on detection performance.
Baseline comparison performed against rule-based systems, logistic regression, random forest, and supervised LSTM models.
findings: num: Proposed SSL and hybrid framework achieves 0.98 precision, 0.90 recall, and 0.96 F1-score on real-world imbalanced transaction data.
num: GNN-based identity modeling reduces false positive rate from 0.19 to 0.04, significantly improving prediction reliability.
num: Combined SSL with contrastive and masked reconstruction reaches 0.96 F1-score versus 0.81 without any self-supervised learning.
num: 17% higher recall, 12% higher precision, and 19% higher F1-score compared to rule-based and supervised fraud detectors.
num: Contrastive learning alone achieves 0.89 F1-score while masked reconstruction alone achieves 0.88 F1-score.
num: Supervised LSTM baseline achieves 0.86 precision, 0.69 recall, and 0.77 F1-score, substantially below the proposed framework.
num: Rule-based systems perform poorly with only 0.28 F1-score and 0.21 false positive rate.
key_figures_tables: Table 1: Dataset Statistics showing 35.2M transactions, 95K fraud cases, 0.27% fraud rate, 187 features.
Table 2: Performance Comparison showing proposed SSL+Hybrid achieves 0.98 precision, 0.96 F1, 0.04 FPR.
Table 3: Effect of GNN-Based Identity Modeling showing GNN reduces FPR from 0.19 to 0.04.
Table 4: Contribution of Self-Supervised Components showing combined SSL achieves 0.96 F1 versus 0.81 without SSL.
Figure 1: Overall System Architecture Diagram showing end-to-end pipeline from raw data to fraud risk score.
Figure 2: Performance Comparison of ML and DL Models showing proposed framework outperforms all baselines.

key_equations.explanation: Temperature-scaled contrastive loss maximizing agreement between augmented views.
Weighted aggregation of base classifier probabilities for final fraud risk score.

definitions.definition: Self-Supervised Learning; a representation learning paradigm using intrinsic data structure without explicit labels.
Graph Neural Network; a neural network that operates on graph-structured data to model relational dependencies.
Long Short-Term Memory; a recurrent neural network architecture for learning long-term sequential dependencies.
A neural network architecture based on self-attention mechanisms for modeling sequential data.
Extreme Gradient Boosting; an ensemble learning method based on sequential decision trees.
Graph Sample and Aggregate; a framework for inductive representation learning on graphs via neighborhood sampling.
Graph Attention Network; a graph neural network variant using attention mechanisms to weight neighbor importance.
Receiver Operating Characteristic Area Under the Curve; a metric evaluating classifier discrimination ability.
False Positive Rate; the proportion of legitimate transactions incorrectly identified as fraud.
Deep Neural Network; a multi-layered neural network for learning high-dimensional feature representations.
Explainable Artificial Intelligence; AI systems designed for human interpretability and transparency.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: The paper introduces a multi-stage fraud detection architecture combining self-supervised learning with graph-based identity modeling, demonstrating that unlabeled transaction data can produce high-quality behavioral embeddings for downstream anomaly detection.
directly_justifies: Combined SSL with contrastive and masked reconstruction achieves 0.96 F1-score on financial fraud detection.
GNN-based identity modeling reduces false positive rate from 0.19 to 0.04.
Proposed framework achieves 0.98 precision and 0.90 recall on 35.2M real-world transactions.
Self-supervised approach reduces dependence on labeled fraud data by leveraging unlabeled transaction sequences.
Stacked ensemble of XGBoost, DNN, and logistic regression effectively fuses multiple behavioral embeddings.
limits: Paper addresses fraud detection in banking transactions, not personal finance management or budgeting concerns.
No evaluation on personal spending data from individual budgeting or expense tracking scenarios.
Anomaly detection focus differs from spending categorization and budget allocation topics in the taxonomy.

limitations: Training hyperparameters, computational costs, and convergence details are not reported. [unacknowledged]
Dataset source and detailed feature descriptions are not clearly specified. [unacknowledged]
No comparison with recent state-of-the-art transformer-based or graph-based fraud detection methods. [unacknowledged]
Federated learning for privacy-preserving multi-institution detection is planned but not yet implemented.
Explainable AI modules for transparency and interpretability are identified as future work.
Online continuous learning for real-time concept drift adaptation is not yet implemented.
